text: Good afternoon. My name is Dina Griffiths, and I'm calling to order the Finance and Operations Committee meeting for October 6th, 2026. I am joined by Mr. John Pepper and Ms. Amy Ricardi. And with that, we do not have public comment today, so we'll move on to the minutes. Do I have a motion to approve the minutes from the September 15th, 2026 Finance and Operations Committee? So moved. Second.

Thank you. It has been moved and seconded by Mr. Pepper and Ms. Ricardi. All those in favor say aye. Aye. Aye. Aye. Approval of the consent agenda. We will now move to that. May I have a motion to approve the consent agenda? I move to approve the consent agenda for the October 6th, 2026 Finance Operations Committee meeting. Thank you. A second? Second.

Thank you. It has been moved to approve the consent agenda by Mr. Pepper and seconded by Ms. Ricardi. All those in favor say aye. Aye. Aye. Aye. We will now move on to our action items, starting with item 5.01, Business and Financial Services revision of Policy 4330, Remedies and Bids and Awards. May I have a motion to approve 5.01?

I move that the Finance and Operations Committee recommend the Loudoun County School Board adopt revised Policy 4330, Remedies and Bids and Awards. Sorry. Second. There we go. Thank you. The motion was made by Mr. Pepper and seconded by Ms. Ricardi. This item is being presented by Ms. Felau, Director of Procurement and Risk Management. Thank you.

There have been no changes since we last presented this to you at your previous meeting where we had discussed this policy. So the red lines still remain as redlined, and the document in it is clean. So like I said, there was no changes. Thank you. Any questions? Any discussion? Ms. Ricardi? Thank you, Madam Chair. So I just had a couple questions. I noticed we've got some feedback now from the public. I don't remember if that was up last time or not.

But I have a couple of questions, I think, for both of these policies, because it's part of the bigger package for procurement, right? So this is the last two, I believe, of the procurement policies that we've been looking at. Is that- These are the ones that are due for review at this time. Okay. So, and we have had a couple of other ones earlier this year. And so I guess one of the questions I had, as I've been looking through and

crosswalking all these policies, one of the reasons why I wanted this to come back to action this time and not go to consent is that I really want to see if we've done a really good job of closing gaps between policies. Number one, so there's no daylight between them. So in the procurement process that we're making sure that we don't have any gaps. I still have some concerns about both of these policies, but for this one in particular,

we got some really good feedback about some accountability pieces of this. So, the summary says that this revision identifies who signs contracts by dollar amount and contract type. But I don't see anywhere in the redline or the clean copy. That is not this policy. Is that the- That's our contract authority policy that has already been through committee and school board. Okay.
It's not 4330? No, it is not 4330. Okay. All right. So I'll ask this one then. In the redline version, I think it's line four about the appeal paragraph. Is there a general appeal?

That was moved. That is now item D in your policy. If we go down, you will see that in item D, it talks about the protest of the award or decision to award. That is your appeal process as it relates to procurement. It was just spelled out in much clearer detail per Virginia Code and the process that is put in place. So it was expanded in Section D and removed as an introduction paragraph. Okay. All right. That's helpful.

And then do we have, maybe it's talking about an administrative appeal process for this? Is that all just covered in that? The process is there's a protest, and in Virginia, there's arbitration. Ms. Ewing can speak to that if we need to. But there's arbitration, there's not mediation. But it is explained in here what the process is for the protest and what happens following the protest.

Okay, that's helpful. And then can we go back to Section A2? By the way, I like the fact that we've got these up here. Like this a lot. This is really helpful, especially when we don't have multiple versions of redlines. I don't think I've seen this one, but sometimes we do, and this is really helpful. So I noticed it has in here the notice of intent to award, but

was that a change? We have the notice of intent to award or notice of award, which is the process we have been following, and there is no change in the policy with this revised policy. We follow that today. The notice of intent to award is issued, and we issue the notice of intent to award to basically start the protest period. There's the 10-day protest period.

Upon successful award, either award by the school board or the award following those 10 days, we then issue the notice of award. That is a process we follow per internal procedures, but per the code, you must do a notice of intent to award or notice of award. And that has been in this policy. Okay. And then does this policy have a companion regulation to it? No, this policy does not have a companion regulation. Okay. Great. Thank you.

Mr. Pepper? Thank you, Madam Chair. And thank you for your work on the policy. I know all these procurement things are very weedy, and they have to follow state code and all sorts of best practices. My question really is about Section C on debarment. And I might actually piggyback off of Ms. Ricardi's question about a regulation here. The whole section, to me, my concern here is the vagary with the debarment period.

In particular, it says that a contractor may be debarred for specified periods of time without specifying the periods of time. Is there a matrix or a decision tree or something we would use to determine what that said period of time is, should a contractor be debarred? I will tell you that routinely, in my experience, we have followed one year of debarment, basically giving them an opportunity. In my experience, I think I've debarred once in 30 years.

Most of the vendors, we work with those vendors and solution through the protest process, cure letters, conversation, and we don't get to the point of debarring someone for failure to perform. It's good that we're not debarring people. I am a big believer that we should have, and it could possibly be a regulation, some sort of matrix or decision tree about what the length of period of debarment should be that accompanies this policy. So I would highly recommend that.

It is also later on in that sentence, in line 72 of the red line version, it mentions for contracting for particular types of supplies, services, insurance, or construction, and my question is, if a contractor is debarred from one of these, are they necessarily debarred from others? Not necessarily debarred or are they debarred? Because I know this question did come up.

Mr. Pepper, Janice Ewing, Deputy Division Counsel. So we had a discussion about that specific language, and I recommended that they keep it in as far as being specific types, because a lot of times, especially looking for construction, you may have someone who wants to bid for a roofing contract, and they're better at painting and flooring. They don't have the requisite expertise. And so while we may need to discourage them from bidding for roofing projects, we still want to encourage them to have other projects.

But you wouldn't want to bar them from all construction with LCPS. So by saying specified types lets you identify the specific type of commodity that they may not be eligible or qualified for. But if we don't do what's called a prequalification process, there isn't really a way to stop people from bidding, and someone could underbid, and if it is an IFB, we would have to accept the lowest bidder. There is a responsibility check, but if they clear all those hurdles, you could

still have an issue. So it's just another avenue for staff to be able to hold vendors accountable for specific types of projects without keeping them from an opportunity. I appreciate that, and thank you for helping clarify the language and why it's written the way it's written. Those are really the two questions I have on the policy. I appreciate your response. Thank you, Mr. Pepper. Per this policy, I know we discussed previously that

you have a lower bid than somebody else who made a bid, and they could protest, but then that person can also rebid to come in lower. We talked about that last time, correct? No, they cannot submit a new bid to come in at a lower price. Oh, they cannot. Once the bid- If it's a low-price IFB, for example- Uh-huh ... they cannot change their price. Okay. RFB, you can negotiate with them to adjust their price, but they can't come in and

say, "Oh my gosh, we just saw this award and realized they bid $1,000 and we bid $2,000. We want to counter-bid now with $1,000." Okay. I just wanted to be clear on that. Also, just for clarity, I did make a motion to, as far as ownership, to change some of the verbiage in here, where it says his or her, to make it their, T-H-E-I-R, to show ownership.

I did that because I was looking at the clean copy and the red line, and it didn't sound right. In the clean copy, you took out his/her a bid. I just want to clean it up and show ownership. It says a bid instead of their bid. So I wanted to go back and do that. So I wanted to make a motion to clean up the policy, and use ownership as far as where you might have taken out

his/her. And I can give you the lines if you're interested. I can give you the lines. Oh, did you want to say something, Ms. Hardy? No, I was going to say that I know we loaded into BoardDocs your motion, and we would just need the committee to formalize your motion and a vote. We can take a vote on that now.

Yeah, and on my amendment to just clean it up to show ownership, because if you do read it, it doesn't read clear. So, have you both read my amendment, or do you want me to read it for you? Madam Chair, can we make a motion for the amendment and have it seconded, and then discuss line numbers? Oh, here, let me read it.

Of course, I don't have it in front of me, so hold on one second. I've got it. Oh, you got it? Okay. All right. So here, you want to read it? Yeah, sure. Thank you. I would like to make a motion on Policy 43330, Remedies in Bid and Awards. I move to amend the motion to replace his/her thoroughly throughout the document with their, T-H-E-I-R, as a possessive

pronoun determiner that shows ownership. Do I have a second? Second. Thank you. Couple questions, Madam Chair. Sure. First, I'm assuming that you're looking to amend the clean version and not the red line version, because if you're replacing his/her, the red line version, they've been removed. Is that correct? That is correct. They were removed in the red line, and the clean version, it just

says a bid. It's not clarifying ownership. So I would like to fix it in the clean version. But if you do look at the red line, you will see that it was red lined to come out. Do you have the line numbers of each? I do. I do. Can you read those off please? I do. Line 14, lines 28 and 29, line 31, and line 35. And anywhere I may have missed in the document, but that's what I have.

Go ahead. I'm reading. Yeah. So I see that you guys have made the changes in the red line to just- Take- ... yes, so it's like the bid or the claim or a bid. Are we standardizing that across all the policies, not just the procurement policies, but what's the nomenclature that we're using generally across all policies right now? I would welcome Ms. Ewing to chime in, but I believe we're doing it to be in line

with the other policies where we removed him, her, his, or we remained silent and did it the way that the red line was shown. Okay. And is that standard for how we're doing it across the board from a legal perspective? That's my understanding. I believe at the last committee meeting, Ms. Willoughby had a little bit of feedback from cabinet, and I think it was discussed across the board of all policies, but I think we are removing the possessiveness or

at least the use of specific pronouns in our policies. If I may. I believe this is the APA language that we don't have to use it. We choose to, but we don't have to. To make the policy sound correct, we can use what I'm adding today, which is the possessive T-H-E-I-R for the policy.

Yes. It's up to the committee on the version that you want to move forward to the full board. Thank you. I guess my question is, I want to make sure that we're being consistent for all our F&O policies along with what we're doing. I guess I'm asking the global question. Is this the process that we're using going forward with all LCPS policies from the school board to as they're coming back through? We're just removing pronouns completely and just going straight to the, in this case, the nouns?

Mr. Hardy, that's my understanding, but I can always verify that. A lot of these go through the legislative committee, and so we can just confirm that that's the process that they are continuing with the other policies, not only ones here, but in other areas. So I can verify just to make sure. That would be really helpful. And it's not that I don't agree with the amendment, it's just I want to make sure that regardless of what we're doing, we're just being consistent across the board, and if this is a new approach that we're taking a policy-wise. Are you seeing this at all in your-

So what I'm seeing is these, where unless it's specific, we're doing things like him or her with the student in other committees, so we're trying to keep it very-- We're basically removing all pronouns, and it reads fine. Truthfully, I believe that the policy without their or his/her reads completely fine at, from both a-- And Ms. Ewing, correct me, from both a legal perspective and a policy perspective.

And for consistency's sake, I think that we should just leave the pronouns as is and not include them for now. And if we do get this through and it is different, and Ms. Ewing comes back with a report, we can always change this at the full board level as well. Well, if I may, when I read the clean copy,

line one, A1, a bidder may withdraw a bid, but the bidder is withdrawing their bid. That's what I'm trying to point out. They're not a bid, not just a random bid. They're withdrawing their bid. So in the lines I provided, it generally it's responding to somebody and showing ownership in particular to this policy. That's why I wanted to clean it up and keep that in there, or put that in

there. So I just want to clarify. I understand, Mr. Hardy, where you are on consistency, but sometimes I feel like show possession and have the language written correctly. Thank you. Ms. Griffiths, if I can add a point of clarification. Sometimes with procurements for multi-awards, they may submit pricing for more than one item, and so they may have a miscalculation on one aspect of it.

So they could withdraw in part, but not the full one. So I just wanted to mention that because they are making their entire bid and not a portion thereof. I just wanted to note that. Mr. Carty. Yes. Okay. So I read through this before, but now that I'm reading it with a different lens, I think there are a couple of places in here where we do need to show possessives, like section B,

it talks about the superintendent's designees. The clarity is it's the superintendent or, and then his and her were taken out, designees. But it's really the superintendent's designees, not designees in general. So I think there may be some places in here where the possession is important to clarify, and I agree also with the bidders, like their claim or

their bid, it does need to be theirs, not just they can't just withdraw any bid- Yeah ... as it's being read. So I think we need to take a look, especially when it comes to procurement, about making sure that as we're changing those pronouns, we're not changing the meaning of the intent by pulling it out. Does that make sense? To me, it does. It may not need to happen everywhere, but it definitely needs to happen when we're claiming about somebody else.

And if I may, these are bids by specific companies. So to say, "Remove a bid," well, was it their bid? What bid are they removing? As Mr. Carty mentioned. So I think in this policy, there are situations where you need to show possession. Thank you. Mr. Pepper.

I'm trying to process this. So for example, there are some things I do agree with, like line 48 does read very strange. Perhaps it'd be better if it said the superintendent or superintendents designees- Yes ... with an extra superintendent in there. But at the same time, I still read it the way that perhaps Ms. Ewing reads it with a bidder may withdraw a bid. Perhaps that bidder has multiple bids and just wants to remove one or one part of one. I like it the way it is, but that's just how I feel.

I really don't know that showing possession is a big deal. It's just cleaning it up. I know you would like to follow the APA guidelines, but it's not always appropriate for certain policies. Sometimes you can take things out and it sounds fine, but to me, when I was reading the clean copy, it did not sound correct.

And as far as consistency, I know we're using the APA guidelines in other areas, and I understand that, but our English language, it should sound like our English language and not take things out and change it around. So with that being said, can we take a vote on this, or you had a second before. Can I have a second again? Second.

Okay, good. So, all those in favor, say aye. Aye. Aye. No. So with that, if we can go ahead and make those changes, I would really appreciate that. And then I guess it'll be coming back to us through action next time? It's on action. You should- Well, you're making the changes, and it's coming back again, so. I think you need to make-

Madam Chair, we have amended the policy. It's an amendment vote. Okay. So it'll be good to go to the board. Okay. We have to vote to approve it, Madam Chair. Well, let's approve it. Sounds great. All right, so we're good on that one. No, we still have to vote to approve it, Madam Chair. We've done the amendment, now we need to go back to the main motion. Okay. Let's go back to the main motion and any other discussion? We will proceed to a vote. All those in favor say aye. Aye. Aye.

Thank you. That should go to the board then. Thank you. Item 5.02, business and financial services revision of Policy 4340, procurement procedures. May I have a motion to approve 5.02? Madam Chair, I move that the Finance and Operations Committee recommend the Loudoun County School Board adopt revised Policy 4340, procurement exceptions.

Second. Thank you. It's been the motion by Mr. Pepper and then seconded by Mr. Carty. This item is being presented by Ms. Villa. Thank you. Once again, there was no changes made in this policy based on comment received from the community. The comments appeared to be more related to transparency in our equitable practices, which are addressed in our standard operating procedures

within LCPS, and the equity council did have a comment regarding SLAM, but we do have Policy 4360 that outlines our SLAM policy. Thank you. Any discussion? Mr. Carty. Okay. So for this policy, I went through and took a look at policies 4310 through 4370, just to do a little bit of a crosswalk, as I'd mentioned before.

I've got about nine different things in here that I want to clarify, but I'm not going to do them here for that. So I guess one of the questions I have on this policy is about the no anti-splitting rule. If you could explain that a little bit more. May I please get a line number where you're at on that? Let me find it.
Sorry. Line 42 to 45 in the administrative exemptions.

I'm not seeing anything related to splitting on those lines. That might be just the ceiling on that. Give me one second. Let me find it. I took notes, but I didn't put the line numbers, which I should have probably done. I can tell you what I'm going for here really quickly. So I want to make sure that--

So Policy 4320 has a rule in there that says there's a 5,000 and a 50,000 limit on, I think, splitting contracts. Those limits are established to determine what method of procurement we can use, and it's for the purchase of like commodities. So if we are purchasing something that is a one-time purchase of $3,000, you can

just do a single quote. If we are purchasing like items that are between five and 50, you must get three written quotes or attempt to get three written quotes. 50 up to 200 is an RFQ, a request for quotes, where we must try to get at least four responses. Above 200,000 is our formal solicitation process, which relates to our IFB and

RFP process. The splitting of purchases generally comes into play to ensure that there is no attempt to try to bypass those limits as established. The key criteria with that, though, is the purchase of like items, not the purchase from a vendor. We could purchase from a vendor $200,000 of something, but as far as a like commodity, it could be $5,000, and it's based on the purchase

of like items. When you have vendors that sell many types of commodities, you could have different contracts for them with different goods or services on it. Okay. So what happens then, I guess, if you have Multiple vendors that you're buying the same product from, but all underneath the $250,000 threshold that we have.

Once again, with the purchase of like items, if we are purchasing, for example, music equipment. We purchase music equipment, and when we open a new school, it exceeds $200,000. Therefore, we do a solicitation. There may be another year where we don't buy that much in equipment if we're not opening a new school. In that case, we would go to the other method of procurement. The likeness is in the fact that we have various criteria. We have percussion and keyboards is one, we have secondary music that is one, and

we have elementary music. Because those instruments vary, they are treated as like commodities in reference to the titles of the bids, as I mentioned. Okay. Thank you. Any other questions? Mr. Pepper. Just really briefly, and you may have already addressed this, the section on the red line between 90 and all the way down to 144 about discrimination, aliens, sex offenders. I assume that's somewhere else.

That is in the regulation that I shared with you as part of your packet for this evening. It's already been added into there. Perfect. Just want to make sure that everyone knows where to find it. Yes, sir. Thank you. If there's no other discussion, we'll proceed to a vote. Yep. All those in favor say aye. Aye. Aye. Thank you. We'll move on to item 5.03, support services approval of capital improvement fund

transfer and supplemental funds, request for VIEW Transition Academy. May I have a motion to approve 5.03? Madam Chair, I move that the Finance and Operations Committee request that the Loudoun County School Board request the Loudoun County Board of Supervisors appropriate $20,039,095.33 from the county-held LCPS contingency fund or other county funding sources available, and transfer

$3,930,904.67 from multiple completed capital projects with available funding to the VIEW Transition Academy project. Further, the completed capital projects identified with an asterisk in the chart on board docs and policy 5.03 are to be closed. Do we have a second? Second. Thank you. The motion has been made and seconded by Mr. Pepper and Ms. Record.

This item will be presented by Mr. Passmore. Thank you. Thank you. So during the information session we had in here, there was a question that Ms. Record had regarding the nature of the contingency fund. So subsequent to that, there was information that was sent to you and other board members with some details as well as the board of supervisors' action items related to that. So, I'm happy to answer any other questions you may have.

Ms. Record. No, thank you. I appreciate the information. So we have the $20 million and just shy of $4 million. How are we making up the gap again on that? Because you're asking for $47. So we currently in the CIP now, we have the remaining dollars that we need to fully fund the project in the CIP. This is supplemental funding that will fully fund the project.

So I'm a big supporter of the VIEW Academy. I just think one of the things we're going to hear really quickly, I've actually already been hearing about it, is the fact that we've got lower enrollment, and we're asking for significantly more money than the original project was initially specced at. And so, I know we're expanding the footprint. I know it's the building, but it's getting renovated and added onto, so big

expansion. I know from here we were starting with 100 students, and we're looking to expand to 500 in that facility. Is that...? I believe ultimately that's the goal. Yep. I just want to make sure that the public, number one, is aware of that, and that can you also, from a transportation perspective, we're busing students to this facility. How is that all working?

Yeah, I can speak a little bit to... Actually, do you mind, Mr. Davies, to chip in? Yes, that is correct. We will be providing transportation to the Transition Academy, and we're working with the group that is organizing that on how that will occur and from where and all that stuff. Is that from base schools or is that from home? That'll be from home. Okay.

Do we have an estimate for the transportation costs for this at this point? Not at this point, no. Okay. If I may add to the discussion, and we sort of discussed this offline, but it went from $24 million to $48 million. Just for clarity

so the public knows why it jumped so much, my understanding is putting state-of-the-art CTE programs in the building. If somebody could give more detail on that for the public so they understand why it jumped, it doubled in cost. Thank you. So, a couple of things I'll say about that is, this program is a brand new program

for LCPS. So, it's much different than, for example, a high school or an elementary school that we currently do where we understand what that program looks like. And this program was expedited through our capital budget program, so we were starting design roughly this time last year when we were actually submitting for that number. So the program hadn't been developed that far, and as the program developed,

we received cost estimates, and the ultimate program included an extensive renovation as well as an addition to the building. Thank you. And also, I'd like to point out with budget issues that we're having, a lot is going into this building, for the transition center, which I totally am for. I guess I have a couple questions. Well, because we're having budget issues and

we're going to have great CTE programs there, is it just going to be specifically for special ed or are other students able to use the facility? My understanding is it's focused on special ed students. Okay. So just special ed. And, probably not going to like this question I'm going to ask.

Because it doubled and we're spending this amount of money on this building, that's going to take away from other schools, if they need renovations or if they need anything. Can you elaborate on that, please? Yeah, I would say, so this is not taking away from any other programs in the capital budget. That's why the county had created this contingency fund for us. They have a contingency fund for their projects, and they recognized back in 2023,

when they established this for us, that these projects do happen and unexpected costs do occur. So the majority of the dollars that are being requested are from that capital contingency fund. And then roughly $4 million of it is being transferred from existing projects that completed with balances where we saw some cost savings. So it will not affect any other projects that we have going on. Thank you. Are there any other questions? Mr. Pepper.

And just for clarification, Mr. Passmore, the Board of Supervisors replenishes this fund on an annual basis? Yes, sir. Thank you. Ms. Record. I would just also like to just make sure that our communications team does a really great job of getting out into the public. I don't know if anybody here is from the comms teams here. But just really doing a great job getting ahead of this with the public and explaining

the incredible value that this is going to have for our students. I think that's going to be really key. As we're getting into a season of budget tightening and just being a little bit more mindful of that, I think we've really got to make sure that we're explaining to the public exactly what the benefits are, who's being served, and why this transition center is such a value to our community in general. So thank you. Thank you. Is there any other discussion?

If not, we will proceed to a vote. All those in favor, say aye. Aye. Aye. Thank you. We can now move on to 5.04, Support Services Town of Leesburg Proffer Funds. May I have a motion to approve 5.04? So moved. Thank you, Ms. Recordi. Second.

Oh, thank you, Mr. Pepper. This item has been moved and seconded by Ms. Recordi and Mr. Pepper. This item is being presented by Mr. Joseph Passarelli, Director of Construction. Thank you. I'm going to substitute for Mr. Passarelli. You have the update. Last, at your September 15 meeting, we reviewed this item. The town of Leesburg collects cash proffers to offset the impact of

new homes being built within the town limits and onto the public school system. Currently, there is an estimated $3 million available for projects, and I believe, Ms. Recordi, you mentioned last week or last meeting that you were going to confer with Ms. Chernov, and so I will defer to you. Ms. Recordi. Thank you, Madam Chair. So, yes, Ms. Chernov has done a really great job.

I know she's talked to Ms. Tate and I think some other folks from operations team as well about what she's looking for. So she'd proposed a couple of different options on this, and her preference is what's called Option B. I know she submitted, although I guess we didn't put it in here as an attachment, but we have a list of those items in here, and I have it pulled up.

It includes an inclusive playground for Loving Elementary School, outdoor learning space for Catoctin Elementary School, the preschool play areas. Oh, I wish I knew all of her- I thought it was on A. No, she wants B, actually. Yeah, because it's just under $3 million, which is what she's looking for. Yep, so she's looking at-

Sorry ... preschool play areas for three of the elementary schools, tennis court lighting for Tuscarora and Loudoun County High School, a walking path and track for Heritage and- Frederick Douglass ... Frederick Douglass, thank you so much. Pickleball court and a volleyball court. HP is Harbour Park Middle School. So the total is $2,248,500. Mm-hmm.

No, she's not asking for this one. She changed her... The estimated amount initially was at $4 million or so. That was the original number we got. But I think after conferring, it's really more like $3 million. So if I may clarify, there is approximately $3 million available, but it's choking me up talking about it. But part of the item does reference a $4 million threshold.

In order to utilize the funds it would be additional monies on top of what the board of supervisors has already approved for capital budget. So in conversation with Mr. Jones in the budget office, we elected to put a threshold of $4 million in your item so that you would not have to go back on the chance that these are cost estimates, project estimates that were submitted by the principals in some instances. And there may be where the cost would increase

slightly once construction and facility scopes it out. And so we wanted to set the bar a little higher for the request for the board of supervisors, so that we did not have to come back to you to ask you to again request the board of supervisors that we needed $2,000 more. So we set the $4 million, but the available monies right now are $3 million. A little over $3 million. Okay. Mr. Pepper. May I ask a few questions on this? First of all, I'm going to say, when you say

board of supervisors, you mean Leesburg Town Council? No, sir. Okay. So these are additional monies coming in for the school system to use, coming from monies the town of Leesburg collected. But because the board of supervisors has funding authority for the county, like they approve the capital budget, the operating budget, we have to go back to them because this is supplemental above and beyond in some instance what we have planned

in our capital budget. We did not plan to put in a pickleball court at Harbour Park, as an example. We did not plan, at this instance, to put outdoor classroom or a preschool play area.
